worksheet.title: Which One Does Not Belong?
worksheet.subtitle: Finding the odd one out
worksheet.learning_goal: I can find the one that does not belong with the others.

parts.title: One does not belong
parts.text: Most of these are the same. One is different. Help Bit find the one that does NOT belong, and circle it.

parts.title: Watch Bit — three circles and one triangle
parts.note: Three are circles. The triangle ▲ does not belong — it is the odd one out.

parts.title: Circle the odd one out
parts.prompt: Three are the same. Circle the one that does not belong.

parts.title: Circle the odd one out
parts.prompt: Three are the same. Circle the one that does not belong.

parts.title: You try
parts.prompt: Find the one that does not belong and circle it.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: To find the odd one out, you decide what matters — here it is the shape. Choosing what matters is called abstraction, and computers do it to spot things that are different.

teacher_guide.title: Which One Does Not Belong?
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key
teacher_guide.footer_topic: 5. Which One Does Not Belong? — Teacher Guide

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children find the one object in a group that does not share the others' attribute. Deciding what matters (here, shape) and ignoring the rest is abstraction — a computational-thinking skill computers use to detect what is different.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children classify objects and notice which one does not belong.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child circles the odd one out.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil/crayon. Optional: a tray of objects where one does not belong, to find by hand first.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: point to ● ● ● ▲. 'Three are circles. Which one is different?' Circle the triangle.
2. GUIDED: do Exercise 1 together — three stars and one circle; circle the circle.
3. YOU TRY: children do Exercise 2 (the triangle), then Exercise 3 (the star) on their own.
4. Connect: 'Computers spot the odd one too — like finding the one photo that does not match.'

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: circling a shape just because it is at the end — ask 'how is it different?'
Simplify: start with two same + one different before four-card groups.
Extend: ask the child to say WHY it does not belong (it is a triangle, the rest are circles).
Movement option: stand three children doing the same action and one doing a different one — who is the odd one out?

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child circles the single odd item in each group and can say what makes the others the same.
